newsitem.title: UK: Hanson completes breakup as energy unit goes solo.
newsitem.headline: Hanson completes breakup as energy unit goes solo.

text.p: Britain's once mighty Hanson Plc turned into a humble building materials company Monday as the former conglomerate completed its four-way split-up with the spin-off of its Energy Group.
Hanson shareholders voted on Friday to approve the final part of the company's break-up.

The plan ended an era that saw Hanson, under takeover specialist Lord Hanson and his late partner Lord White, become a star performer in the 1980s as it grew into one of Britain's largest conglomerates.

But with a stock market that showed its mistrust of conglomerates by sharply marking down their shares, Hanson last January announced that it would tear itself up into separate tobacco, chemicals, energy and building companies.
Energy has two main parts, U.S.-Australian Peabody Coal, the world's largest private coal producer, and Eastern, Britain's fourth-largest electricity generator and distribution business.

The energy company's shares rose Monday after the company reported a 38 percent rise in operating profit, to 138 million British pounds ($224 million) in the three months to December 31 when Energy Group was still part of Hanson.

The debut of Energy Group on the London Stock Exchange coincided with American Electric Power Co. Inc.'s agreement to buy Yorkshire Electricity Group for about $2.4 billion in a bid with another U.S. utility, Public Service Co. of Colorado.
The offer triggered renewed takeover speculation in the electrity sector and helped push Energy Group's shares up 27-1/2 pence (44 cents) to 552-1/2 pence ($8.90).
The price gives the new company a market value of nearly 2.9 billion pounds ($4.7 billion) compared with less than 1.9 billion pounds ($3.1 billion) for what remains of Hanson.
Hanson earlier spun off its former Imperial Tobacco and Millennium Chemicals units in a bid to streamline its widely diversified operations.

"With all the demergers completed successfully, we can now give full attention to building for the future," said Lord Hanson, who formed the former conglomerate and who remains chairman of the building materials company.
